Diego / Hannah — notes for the packet we will hand back to Claire: 

1) Dedicated capacity allocation model:
- Dedicated nodes are provisioned as customer-bound pools. For Dedicated purchases we allocate entire GPU devices to the customer's container(s) using device assignment (via Kubernetes device plugin + node selectors) — we do not colocate unrelated tenants on the same physical GPU device.
- Where MIG is used it is an opt-in configuration for a customer that purchases a MIG-shaped profile; we do not enable MIG by default across shared Dedicated assignments. When MIG is used we record the MIG slice id and bind only to that slice. Attached sample config shows kubelet flags and plugin params.

2) Runtime isolation and namespaces:
- Each model server runs inside its own container and process namespace. GPU access is constrained by cgroup/device ACLs and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES mapping; there is no shared GPU process between tenants.
- KV-cache (runtime key-value cache used to store token KV for decoding) lives in process memory managed by the model server process and the per-process memory region is not mapped to other tenants. We persist KV only to ephemeral local disk for checkpointing during in-flight upgrade operations; that persistence is encrypted at rest and scoped to the tenant id. Ephemeral persistence is deleted and overwritten on restart.

3) KV eviction / zeroing behavior:
- KV eviction policy: LRU per tenant + size caps. Eviction never promotes a tenant's cache into another tenant namespace.
- On process termination we zero GPU buffers using a single-pass overwrite pattern before releasing the device memory back to the kernel (we also call CUDA API memoryFree and then explicitly scrub mapped host pages where possible).

4) Noisy neighbor and preemption handling:
- For Dedicated we enforce reservation guarantees and do not preempt other tenants within the same reserved pool. For shared-host inference tiers we rely on admission control and per-tenant throttles; preemption is handled by prioritized scheduling.

5) Evidence we can supply (sanitized):
- Allocation snapshot (node, GPU id, tenant id) — sample MIG allocation config attached.
- KV isolation test run (commands and CSV of reads/writes showing namespace separation).
- Memory scrub logs (short excerpt) and the script we run for zeroing.

If Claire needs kernel-level perf traces we'll need to coordinate transfer; otherwise the sanitized CSV + allocation snapshot + PDF attestation should cover SIG control objectives for runtime isolation.

— Rishi

Short summary:
- Dedicated = device-exclusive by default. MIG slices only when customer requests a MIG-shaped profile; slices are bound to a single customer and recorded.
- KV cache is per-process/tenant. We do ephemeral disk checkpointing only for upgrade/resume; checkpoint files are encrypted and removed after use.
- Eviction and zeroing steps are automated in the runtime: LRU eviction within tenant namespace; memory scrub on free.
